① SYMPTOM (Alex, v0.47.0, 2026-09-05): 'The auth field on Interface is a mechanism enum, not an authorization role. Natural to put the role gate there and it hard fails the whole bulk write. Real roles have to live in prose + actor edges.' ② PRECEDENT: question:058f1891de605d77 and dec:pairing-role-placement — `auth` is DELIBERATELY a mechanism, because it is part of the seam-pairing key (base-compatibility = medium + transport_security + auth): a consumer requiring oauth2 must not pair with a provider offering none. schema/structure.yaml:92: 'How the caller proves who it is' — authentication.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) a naming trap — `auth` is read as authorization by a software engineer, and the description is not seen until the enum refuses; (b) the real need (WHO MAY ACCESS — roles) has no vocabulary anywhere, so the nearest-sounding field takes the hit; (c) the hard-fail of the whole batch is a separate matter (#5, dec:bulk-is-all-or-nothing-with-per-item-findings) and not this field's fault. ④⑤ MEASURED: schema grep — the only `role` enums are AUTHORED_BY.role (author/reviewer/approver: design authorship) and TRIGGERS.role (process influence); Actor's only edge is INTERACTS_WITH (Actor -> *), which carries no role. req:vocabulary-covers-personnel — 'which role performs a function ... has nothing to project from' — is DEFERRED. So (b) is TRUE: authorization has no home, and (a) is the trigger that makes it land on `auth`. (c) is true and handled separately.

⑥ CLASS: a broad word naming a narrow enum while the word's other common meaning is unmodelled. Would renaming fix the class? No — the roles would still have nowhere to go. Would the personnel vocabulary fix it? Yes, and it is deferred by Anthony's word. FIX SHAPES, ranked: (1) cheap and honest now — the `auth` description (and the enum refusal) say 'authentication mechanism; for WHO may access, there is no field yet (req:vocabulary-covers-personnel, deferred) — record roles as Actor INTERACTS_WITH plus prose'; (2) the real fix is the deferred requirement, Anthony's call; (3) renaming `auth` to `authentication` is breaking and buys little without (2). ⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: how many users hit this — one report; Alex calls it 'a common first attempt', which is a prediction, not a count.
properties.value: {"auth_is":"authentication mechanism, part of the pairing key (dec:pairing-role-placement)","authorization_roles_home":"none; req:vocabulary-covers-personnel deferred","trigger":"naming trap","fixes":["description+refusal point to the deferred req and the Actor workaround","personnel vocabulary (owner call)","rename (breaking, low value alone)"]}
